title: Rabbi Chanina Torteya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 3:5: “Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha in the name of Rabbi Chiyya bar Va: Rabbi Chanina Tarteya ruled in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.” In Jerusalem Talmud Peah 3:7: “Rabbi Yonah, Rabbi Chanina Torteya in the name of Chizkiyah: It is written, ‘And their father gave them gifts.’” In Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 1:5 the statement is cited in the name of Rabbi Chananyah Tarteya. At the end of Jerusalem Talmud Terumot, chapter 7: Rabbi Chanina Torteyah in the name of Rabbi Yannai, concerning an onion of terumah that was uprooted; in [Nedarim 57b](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.57b.3), Rabbi Chanina Teritaah transmits the statement in Rabbi Yannai’s name, and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha resolved [the question] for Yishmael of Kefar Yama from it. In Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 10:6: Rabbi Chanina Tirta in the name of Rabbi Hoshaya: “bulb vegetables with bulb vegetables — a kind in its own kind.” In [Menachot 48a:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.48a.9): “Rabbi Chanina Terita recited a baraita” (Dikdukei Soferim: Tirta). In [Temurah 29a:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Temurah.29a.7) and 31a: “Rabbi Chanina Teritaah recited a baraita before Rabbi Yochanan.” In [Keritot 9a:29](https://www.sefaria.org/Keritot.9a.29) he asked Rabbi Yochanan.[^3] Seder HaDorot, under the entry Rabbi Chanina ben Toreta, cites a story about him, how he was a gentile and converted through his animal; this story is cited in Pesikta Rabbati, piska Parah, under the name of Rabbi Yochanan ben Toreta.

notes.text: Saved Guggenheimer Berakhot3:5 fully writes Shimon ben Elazar, not ben Abba. Saved Guggenheimer English Terumot10:6 calls חסית bulb vegetables, not lettuce. All Torteya/Tarteya/Tirta/Teritaah variants and the Chanina/Yochanan ben Toreta story contrast remain; reciting a baraita is not an automatic Tannaitic-era assignment.

Guggenheimer Berakhot 3:5 directly writes Shimon ben Elazar, and Guggenheimer’s English Terumot 10:6 gives bulb vegetables. These support the retained corrections without collapsing the Torteya/Tarteya/Tirta/Teritaah forms or Chanina into Yochanan ben Toreta. The exact Dikdukei Soferim and Seder HaDorot editions were not inspected; a reciter occurrence is not an automatic tannaitic-era assignment.

Menachot gives Rabbi Chanina Tirata as a reciter, Temurah has Rav Chananya Teritaah in the Hebrew, and Keritot gives Rabbi Chanina Tirnaah as a questioner. Each passage is linked under its own name form.
